taxonomic_note: Accepted species verified with Kew/POWO and ITIS.
look_here_first: Find the VERY SHORT fuzzy or bristly flowering branches, often several (approximately 5–9) near the upper axis rather than one or two broad eyebrows. Each branch carries awned spikelets, giving a small tufted or starburst appearance. It is NOT enough to see 'a fuzzy grass' — photograph one entire culm and then the narrow hairy branch close up.
project_tracker_diagnostic: small perennial bunchgrass, often under about 50 cm; leaves narrow, often wavy or curled, crowded toward the base but also cauline; terminal racemelike panicle with roughly 5–9 short condensed lateral branches; branches short and densely pubescent with conspicuous awns; clusters of several spikelets with woolly bases; smooth dark nodes on slender weak culms

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Austin Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County explicitly records Bouteloua rigidiseta. Travis — Fowler (2002) documents Bouteloua rigidiseta as abundant in flat plots at Shield Ranch in western Travis County. Williamson — UT Austin Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment of Bouteloua rigidiseta.

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. rigidiseta typically has several (often about 5–9) SHORT bristly/awned units near the top. Blue grama has only about 1–3 long curved combs. Sideoats grama carries many short pendant oats down a much longer axis. Red grama has narrower, more appressed, often purplish branches and awned spikelets; color alone is not sufficient. If an entire culm/branch cannot be resolved, keep Bouteloua sp.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: TEXAS GRAMA: locate a small perennial tuft with usually 6–8(–10) short (~10 mm) one-sided, wedge-like BRISTLY flowering branches spaced along a short axis. Under a hand lens, each branch has relatively FEW spikelets rather than the 20–50 crowded comb spikelets of hairy grama. Confirm the 3-awned fertile lemma and separate longer-awned sterile lemma.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form_and_flowering_architecture: Caespitose perennial with culms about 10–50 cm and leaf blades about 4–12(–17) cm by 1–2 mm in Kew GrassBase. Regional Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas describes 6–8(–10) flowering branches, each about 1 cm; contrast B. curtipendula's many (>25) short branches distributed along a much longer axis.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_collar: Ligule a short fringe of hairs, not a long free membrane; auricles absent. The cited Kew species treatment does not supply a secure numeric ligule length; measure true inside blade/sheath junction with 1-mm scale and keep adjacent sheath/blade hairs distinct. Do not borrow a length from another Bouteloua.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet: Spikelets approximately 2.5–4 mm in Go Botany. One fertile lower floret and a rudimentary upper sterile floret; avoid measuring long awns as spikelet body.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.glumes: Kew GrassBase: lower glume ~2–3.5 mm, one-veined, linear; upper glume ~2.5–4 mm, one-veined, often ciliate on keel, apically two-toothed and carrying a short awn ~1–2.5 mm. Do not call the glumes awnless.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.fertile_lemma_and_awns: Kew GrassBase: fertile lemma body ~2.5–4 mm, three-veined and three-awned; principal awn ~1.5–2 mm, lateral awns ~1 mm. Separate the three lemma awns from the upper-glume awn and from the longer awns of the reduced sterile floret.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.sterile_floret: One upper rudimentary sterile floret, its lemma three-awned; Kew reports upper sterile lemma awns ~5–10 mm. Their long bristles are NOT the same as the shorter fertile lemma awns. Show both florets separated in the macro lesson.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Sideoats grama (B. curtipendula) has far more small branches (often 20–50) along a long axis; hairy grama (B. hirsuta) has only a few long combs packed with many spikelets and a distal bare rachis projection; red grama (B. trifida) has thin appressed branches with a different three-awn arrangement. Blue grama (B. gracilis) has a few broader eyebrows. Count branches on ONE complete culm and dissect a mature spikelet.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — VERY SHORT BRISTLY COMBS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Several ~1-cm flowering branches, not long grama eyebrows
field_id_short_tiles.details: On ONE attached flowering culm count usually 6–8(–10) short, one-sided bristly branches near the upper axis. A full culm and 1-cm scale are needed to distinguish these from the longer combs of blue or hairy grama; existing target photo supports the gross fuzzy-head clue, not a measured count.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD CUE VISIBLE; SCALED FULL CULM NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED TUFT AND TRUE HAIR LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Small perennial tuft; short fringe of hairs at the inner collar
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published Kew description: caespitose perennial, flowering culms approximately 10–50 cm, narrow blades about 1–2 mm wide. Expose the INNER blade–sheath junction to see the short hair-fringe ligule; no reliable species-specific ligule length is established here. Do not call marginal blade hairs a ligule or infer a rhizome from a cropped head.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT A SINGLE MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelet body about 2.5–4 mm; fertile plus reduced sterile floret
field_id_short_tiles.details: An intact one-sided branch carries several laterally compressed spikelets. In one ripe 2.5–4 mm spikelet, identify the lower bisexual fertile floret and the reduced upper sterile floret. Measure the body separately from projecting awns. This anatomy is not resolved in the existing whole-head photos.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower ~2–3.5 mm; upper ~2.5–4 mm and itself short-awned
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase describes one-veined lower and upper glumes; the upper may be ciliate on its keel, two-toothed at the apex, and have its OWN ~1–2.5 mm awn. Photograph each glume with its attachment and 1-mm scale. Do not confuse an upper-glume awn with an awn arising from either lemma.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · TWO LEMMAS, DIFFERENT AWN LENGTHS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma 3-awned; reduced sterile lemma has longer awns
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published fertile lemma body ~2.5–4 mm, with three relatively short awns (central ~1.5–2 mm; laterals ~1 mm). The reduced upper sterile lemma is also three-awned, often with much longer ~5–10 mm awns. A fuzzy branch may show many awns from DIFFERENT florets: count them only after dissecting one mature spikelet and tracing their insertion.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · TEXAS GRAMA OR LOOK-ALIKE?
field_id_short_tiles.short: Very short bristly branches versus sideoats, blue, hairy and red gramas
field_id_short_tiles.details: Sideoats grama has many short branches down a much longer central axis; blue grama usually 1–3 longer curved eyebrows; hairy grama only a few longer densely spikeleted combs, often with a distal bare extension; red grama has slender appressed units. Use matched mature branches and a dissected spikelet. Existing comparison panels depict OTHER species, not rigidiseta anatomy. Keep Bouteloua sp. if branch and lemma characters cannot be resolved.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISON LESSON — MATCHED SCALED PHOTOS NEEDED
